readonly.py:365-368 raises unless the char after `--` is absent or ord<=32 or ==127. This matches MySQL's documented rule (and sql_lex.cc my_isspace||my_iscntrl check): `--` starts a comment only when followed by whitespace or a control character (0-31, 127, plus space 32). Other following characters are refused, which is the conservative boundary. End-of-input is treated as a comment, which is consistent with MySQL. Based on the documented rule; I did not run MySQL. The rejection line concerns /*M! and is unrelated.

readonly.py:342 applies the backslash-escape branch only when quote != '`'. Inside backticks the scanner treats only a doubled backtick as an escape (347-353). This matches the MySQL docs, where a backslash inside a backtick identifier is literal and only a doubled backtick escapes. It also matches sqlglot's MySQL tokenizer as I recall it (IDENTIFIER_ESCAPES is the backtick, STRING_ESCAPES includes the backslash only for strings). I did not read sqlglot's source in the view, so that part is from memory. The rejection in the item concerns /*m! comments and is unrelated.

readonly.py:347-350 inside a quoted run of quote char q (any of ', ", `), a following identical char advances i by 2 and continues, treating it as an escaped literal. This matches MySQL docs: 'a quote inside a string quoted with q may be written as q q', and likewise for backtick identifiers and double-quoted strings/identifiers (ANSI_QUOTES only changes meaning, not the doubling rule). The rejection about /*m! concerns line 356, not this claim.
